key_insight: CompactionRL teaches long-horizon agentic LLMs to survive context-window limits by jointly learning how to act and how to summarize past interactions for continuation.
engineering_relevance: The method is directly useful for building practical coding and agent systems that must run across long trajectories without losing progress when context must be compressed.
method: Jointly optimize task execution and summary generation in RL.
Use token-level loss normalization to balance compact summaries and actions.
Apply cross-trajectory generalized advantage estimation to learn from compacted rollouts.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, CompactionRL improves open-model Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0, including gains of 7.0/3.1 points for GLM-4.5-Air and 5.5/6.8 points for GLM-4.7-Flash.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of learned summaries, so compaction errors or poor credit assignment could still degrade long-horizon training.
paper_title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
